item.title: China Coast Guard expels Japanese boat intruding into waters of Diaoyu Dao
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
BEIJING, Nov. 27 (Xinhua) -- The China Coast Guard (CCG) expelled a Japanese fishing boat that had intruded into the territorial waters of China's Diaoyu Dao on Thursday. The CCG vessels took necessary measures to warn and expel it in accordance with the law, said Jiang Lue, a spokesperson for the CCG. Noting that Diaoyu Dao and its affiliated islands are China's inherent territory, the spokesperson urged the Japanese side to immediately stop all infringement and provocative acts in relevant waters. The CCG will continue to conduct rights-protection and law-enforcement operations in the territorial waters of Diaoyu Dao and its affiliated islands, and safeguard China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, Jiang said.

item.title: Chinese, Russian militaries hold strategic consultation via video link
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
BEIJING, Nov. 26 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese and Russian militaries held a strategic consultation via video conference on Thursday, pledging to strengthen communication and coordination to jointly safeguard international and regional security and stability. The two sides exchanged views on implementing the consensus reached by the two countries' heads of state and on advancing the sustained development of military-to-military relations, according to a statement released by China's Ministry of National Defense. They also held an in-depth exchange of views on the international and regional situation, according to the statement.

item.title: Japan should accelerate disposal process of its abandoned chemical weapons: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 -- "If Japan is unwilling to clean up the chemical weapons left behind during its aggression against China, how can it thoroughly root out the legacy of militarism?" said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a press conference on Thursday. According to reports, China released a documentary titled Return Our Clean Land on Japanese Abandoned Chemical Weapons (ACWs) on November 23, which was screened concurrently during the Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention. Some analysts point out that because Japan has dragged its feet on the destruction process under various pretexts, large quantities of its ACWs remain undisposed of to this day. The spokesperson noted that this year marks the 80th anniversary of the opening of the Tokyo Trial and the 29th anniversary of the entry into force of the Chemical Weapons Convention. During World War II, the invading Japanese forces developed and used chemical weapons against the Chinese people, committing untold crimes against humanity. "The documentaryReturn Our Clean Landdraws on extensive historical records, witness testimonies, and reflections and confessions from Japanese personnel. It recreates the heinous crimes of Japanese aggressors, reveals the lasting harm caused by Japan's ACWs, and underlines that the complete and thorough destruction of Japanese ACWs is a historical, political and legal responsibility that Japan must not shirk,"he said. Chen further pointed out that the Japanese government has long been passive and perfunctory on the issue of its ACWs, delaying the destruction process under various pretexts. Its political commitment to "complete and thorough destruction at an early date" risks becoming an empty promise. Worse still, Japanese right-wing forces, in defiance of international justice and human conscience, blatantly claim that the ACWs have gradually become "not harmful" and that "the legal statute of limitations for liability have passed". "Historical crimes must not be evaded, and responsibilities and obligations must not be shunned. We urge the Japanese side to provide effective information on burial sites at the earliest date, allocate more manpower, and accelerate the disposal process, so that the hazardous Japanese ACWs can be fully destroyed at an early date, and the Chinese people can live on a clean land," the spokesperson stressed.

item.title: Japan disrupts peace and tranquility in Asia-Pacific: Defense Spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
BEIJING, Nov. 26 -- "We require the Japanese side to stop fueling tensions over the South China Sea issue. Any attempt to challenge China's sovereign rights and interests and undermine regional peace and stability will not succeed," said Senior Colonel Chen Xi, spokesperson for China's Ministry of National Defense (MND), at a regular press conference on Thursday. According to reports, the National Institute for Defense Studies under Japan's Ministry of Defense recently released the so-called China Security Report 2027. The report explicitly recommends Japan to sustain its presence in the South China Sea, strengthen minilateral cooperation with its allies and partners, and oppose China's unilateral change to the status quo by force or coercion. Japan's Ambassador to the Philippines recently stated that Japan will provide the Philippines with coastal surveillance radars and surveillance UAVs through the Official Security Assistance program. In response to the reports, the spokesperson pointed out that under the disguise of academic research, Japan, in this report, whitewashes its moves to meddle in the South China Sea issue and stoke tensions across the Asia-Pacific, and smears China's legitimate law-enforcement operations. This is yet another testament to the Japanese authorities' ambition to build up its armed forces and break free from the "exclusively defense-oriented" principle. The international community should stay highly vigilant against this. He also stressed that Nanhai Zhudao is China's inherent territory. Japan is not a party to the South China Sea issue, and is therefore in no position to make irresponsible remarks on it. During WWII, Japan committed numerous crimes in China, including the illegal occupation of China's islands and reefs in the South China Sea, which inflicted untold sufferings on China and the Chinese people. "In recent years, using so-called external threats as an excuse, the Japanese side has incited security anxiety among neighboring countries, supplied weapons and equipment to regional states including the Philippines, formed exclusive military cliques, and sought to enhance its military presence in the South China Sea by provoking confrontation," said the spokesperson, adding that, "Such moves have harmed the shared interests of regional countries and disrupted peace and tranquility in the Asia-Pacific."

item.title: Xi, Pakistani president exchange congratulations over joint spaceflight mission
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari exchanged congratulations on Wednesday on the joint spaceflight mission carried out by astronauts from the two countries. In his message, Xi said the joint space exploration of astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries, as well as another important achievement in bilateral cooperation. Xi said China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to champion peaceful use of outer space and deepen space cooperation.

item.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 spaceship to Tiangong space station with first foreign astronaut on board
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
The Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Minggang) JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China launched the Shenzhou-24 crewed spaceship on Wednesday, sending three astronauts, including a Pakistani payload specialist, to its orbiting Tiangong space station. The spaceship, atop a Long March-2F carrier rocket, blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. The astronauts aboard the spaceship are mission commander and spacecraft pilot Tang Hongbo, flight engineer Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first-ever foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong. The Shenzhou-24 mission marks the first joint flight consisting of Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program.
